dedupe_keys.name: mlit social infrastructure information platform 社会資本情報フラットフォーム bridges tunnels dams sluices ports airports treatment plants with inspection grades by prefecture

description: The Social Infrastructure Information Platform (trial version) of Japan's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism aggregates basic and maintenance information on public infrastructure so that facilities can be browsed and compared across owners. Contents: GeoJSON files per prefecture for 18 facility types: road bridges, pedestrian bridges, tunnels, rock and snow sheds, large culverts and gantry signs; dams, sabo (erosion control) works, sluice gates and sluice pipes; port mooring facilities; urban parks; airports; aids to navigation; government buildings; sewage treatment plants; and water purification plants. Each record carries the facility name, owner (national, prefectural, municipal or expressway company), prefecture and municipality, coordinates, year completed or opened, dimensions such as bridge length and width, and for road structures the overall inspection grade (I to IV) and inspection year; the Tokyo bridge file alone holds 635 bridges. Producer: MLIT, compiling data from road, river, port, airport, sewerage and water supply administrators. Coverage: all 47 prefectures for most types; files were last updated in 2021 and 2022. Format and access: GeoJSON downloads from the G-Spatial Information Center CKAN and a web viewer at ipf.mlit.go.jp. Free under the platform's own terms of use. Caveats: it is a trial platform and coverage differs by facility type and owner, municipal bridges are incomplete, and field names are in Japanese. Simulation uses: an asset and condition inventory for bridge and tunnel risk ranking, seismic and flood exposure of dams, plants and ports, and network vulnerability studies that weight links by structure condition. Related records: National Land Numerical Information roads (data-japan-ksj-roads-n01) and water supply facilities (data-japan-ksj-water-supply-facilities-p21).
